extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, congressional staff, policymakers, journalists, and the public (including victims' families and stakeholders in the opioid crisis)
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a U.S. House hearing examining Purdue Pharma, OxyContin, and the Sackler family focused on corporate conduct, accountability, marketing practices, regulatory responses, and remedies for opioid victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate risk labeling and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: The package insert or labeling for the product has changed over time; in 2001 the FDA changed labeling to include a black-box warning calling attention to the risk of abuse, misuse, and addiction specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should ensure product labels and inserts accurately reflect addiction/abuse risk and update labeling as scientific understanding evolves. Example: 2001 black-box warning inclusion is cited as a corrective measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory prescriber education
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue, along with other companies, proposed that prescriber education be mandatory in order to prescribe controlled substances and that doing so be linked to the registration process for DEA certification (discussed in REMS development around 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require training for prescribers of opioids tied to licensure/DEA registration to ensure competence before issuing prescriptions; cited as a major policy recommendation to reduce inappropriate prescribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and community education & prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue supported public awareness campaigns and third-party education organizations, putting forward key messages related to safe storage of medicines and proper disposal of prescription medicines; supported programs directed at schoolchildren (EverFi) to raise awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should fund and support community-directed education (patients, families, school programs) emphasizing safe storage/disposal and addiction risks because many diverted medicines originate from friends/family medicine cabinets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The company played a lead role in the development of the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy and participated in proposing measures (circa 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pharmaceutical companies should actively engage in REMS processes and propose/implement meaningful risk mitigation actions rather than resist regulatory safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict aggressive marketing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Ending the company's use of tactics like detailing (sales representatives targeting prescribers) and eliminating speakers' programs; CEO decision in 2017 to stop sales-rep-based promotion of opioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should cease aggressive sales tactics that encourage overprescribing (detailing, targeting high-prescribers, incentive programs). Stopping these tactics is presented as a necessary reform to curb inappropriate prescribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public document disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOJ settlement requires Purdue to set up a public document repository containing documents Purdue handed over to DOJ; committee members want family-held documents contributed as well and seek commitments from the Sacklers to turn over relevant documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full transparency — including timely public access to documents related to marketing, internal communications, and the investigation — is a standard for accountability. Delays or exclusions (e.g., family-held documents excluded until after bankruptcy) are criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of wrongdoing and criminal accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether executives or family members admit wrongdoing or bear criminal liability is scrutinized; Purdue pleaded guilty to three felonies in federal district court, but family members did not admit wrongdoing or spend time in jail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal admissions and criminal accountability are considered key measures of responsibility. The presence or absence of admissions/jail time is used as an evaluative criterion for corporate and individual accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate compensation to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate over whether offered sums (e.g., $3 billion from the family in bankruptcy) and bankruptcy processes provide adequate and equitable compensation to opioid victims and their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fairness by comparing victim needs and societal harms to the amounts and structures proposed in settlements/bankruptcy; criticism arises when settlements appear to shield wealthy parties while providing limited recovery to victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate governance and board responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns that the Sackler family and board exercised de facto executive control (board operating as de facto CEO), directing marketing strategies and company operations, including hiring more sales reps and targeting prescribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards should exercise oversight and not be instruments for profit-maximizing directives that risk public harm; governance failures are evaluated by examining internal directives, emails, and strategic campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid targeting high-risk prescribers and vulnerable communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing deliberately targeted high-prescribers and vulnerable/rural communities (e.g., campaigns to turbo-charge sales such as 'Evolve to Excellence' and marketing to rural parts of states like Virginia), which led to increased prescription rates and community harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing strategies must not focus on prescribers or communities likely to produce disproportionate or harmful prescribing patterns. Targeting high-volume prescribers and understating risks in vulnerable areas is flagged as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce formulation barriers to reduce abuse potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that all medicines in the class (controlled-release and immediate-release opioids) have barriers introduced to make them less susceptible or attractive as drugs of abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support reformulations/technological safeguards that reduce diversion and misuse; design and regulatory actions should aim to lower abuse potential of opioid products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest marketing claims about addiction risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Company marketed OxyContin as having much lower addiction risk (e.g., less-than-1% addiction claim) which sharply contrasted with reality; Purdue pled guilty in 2007 for misbranding based on such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing materials must accurately reflect addiction risks; misbranding or downplaying addiction potential is a core evaluative failure. Historical examples (2007 misbranding) are used to demonstrate misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for addiction treatment and community recovery programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue's Office of Corporate Social Responsibility supported community-based programs aimed at education, addiction recovery, retraining, and reentry to the workforce in states affected by the epidemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate contributions to treatment, recovery, and workforce reentry are viewed as part of remediation; evaluate scope, geographic focus, and sufficiency of such support when assessing corporate responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and evaluate patient assistance programs for unintended effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient savings cards (intended to expand access) were tracked and evaluated because they were powerful ways to keep patients on opioids longer; committee concerns that such programs can prolong opioid use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess patient-assistance programs for whether they promote appropriate access or inadvertently encourage long-term opioid dependency; monitoring and evaluation are required to prevent abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote non-opioid pain management and access to alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy for a multidisciplinary approach to pain management (nerve blocks, physical therapy, behavioral/cognitive therapy, rehabilitation, biofeedback) and removing barriers that limit access to nonpharmacologic options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical and policy approaches should prioritize non-opioid modalities before initiating opioid therapy and improve patient access to these alternatives (insurance coverage, availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral responsibility and ethical conduct beyond legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for the Sackler family to accept moral responsibility (not merely legal denials); critique of passive phrasing ('has been associated with abuse') and demand for explicit acknowledgment of the family's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include ethical/moral accountability (public apologies, acknowledgment of harm) in addition to legal outcomes. Avoiding responsibility through language or legal shield is criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pre-bankruptcy asset stripping / 'milking' the company
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that family members discussed 'milking the company' and removed millions/billions in profits prior to bankruptcy, raising concerns that bankruptcy is being used to shield assets from victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize pre-bankruptcy distributions and transfers for signs of asset stripping; equitable remedy requires that corporate reorganizations not be structured to protect wealthy insiders at victims' expense.
